reason: Prefer a physical DOM list/listitem ownership shape over aria-owns because owned-node accessibility order can reorder/duplicate unexpectedly. No WordPress write is authorized by this file.

items: 2004–2005: János precíz tervei alapján épült meg a kert, amely cégünk értékrendjét tükrözi.
Több évtizedes gondoskodás: nemcsak az induláskor, hanem a mindennapi fenntartásban és a növények szakszerű ápolásában is hű társunk.
Folyamatos megújulás: János lélegzetelállító formára nyírt növénykülönlegességeivel folyamatosan fejleszti a teret.

last_trusted_target: One p.af-review-text contains five span siblings: intro, point1, point2, point3, final. The middle three have no list/listitem semantics.
preferred_candidate_shape: Preserve the existing paragraph and all five visible text spans. Replace only the exact contiguous point1+point2+point3 substring with one inline span role=list wrapper containing those same three point spans in the same order, each with role=listitem. Intro and final remain siblings outside the list wrapper.
why_preferred: Natural DOM ownership matches reading order instead of importing nodes through aria-owns.
No visible copy is duplicated or rewritten.
The Atomic paragraph remains the same owner/type; no full Elementor save is needed.
The three original point spans can retain their current classes/content and therefore have the best chance of preserving existing bullet presentation.
Rollback can be one exact inverse replacement of the wrapper boundary.

Exact live page256 WPVibe profile is ncsnorbert+20260914-4@gmail.com; current site/quota known; D11 reserve preserved.
Fresh COMPLETE LIVE ID35 state and page256 saved bytes/SHA/JSON reconciled.
Fresh saved-data search returns one compact exact boundary containing all three point spans contiguously and no intro/final/protected unrelated review text.

Fresh rendered/computed-style or exact CSS-owner inspection proves the point visuals do not depend on each point being a direct child of p.af-review-text; if a direct-child selector is the winner, either prove an exact page-local replacement selector after carrier PASS or abort this strategy.
Fresh active-Panasonic source/target AX proves target currently lacks list1/items3 and source still has exactly list1/items3.
candidate_markup_rules: Use an inline element such as span as the physical role=list owner so it remains valid inside the existing p owner.
Do not use display:contents as an accessibility shortcut; browser semantic retention is not assumed.
Do not use aria-owns when the physical wrapper path is safely available.
Do not introduce duplicate text, hidden mirror lists, nested block ul/li inside p, new focusability, IDs unless fresh CSS/AX proof requires them, or script reparenting.
Preserve every existing point span class and exact text byte sequence.
one_transaction_requirement: The complete point1+point2+point3 substring must be replaced in one guarded match-once edit. If the boundary is not unique/complete, do not split wrapper creation across calls.
immediate_readback: page JSON valid and only expected local saved-data delta
visible Panasonic review text/order and bullet presentation unchanged
active Panasonic AX: exactly one list and three listItems in source order
intro and final text remain outside the list in reading order
tab accessible name, tabPanel role/name/ownership and previous/next controls unchanged
abort_or_rollback_if: fresh boundary contains more protected text than the three point spans
current visual styling requires direct p > span ownership and no independently proven page-local selector can preserve it
wrapper changes line breaks/bullet geometry/spacing materially
AX loses/reorders/duplicates intro, points or final text
tabPanel/body reading order or accessible name changes
429/5xx/ambiguous write result until exact readback resolves it
fallback: If physical wrapper proof fails, keep review_points_semantics OPEN. The old aria-owns idea remains diagnostic context only and is not an automatic fallback write.
